scenarios.label: Baseline (as operated)
scenarios.note: Fuel burn as observed, priced at Indonesian domestic industrial rates.

scenarios.label: B40 drop-in biodiesel
scenarios.note: Drop-in, no vessel modification. Already the mandated blend on land.

scenarios.label: B100 / HVO drop-in
scenarios.note: Drop-in after fuel-system checks. Near-zero sulphur and lower black carbon.

scenarios.label: Bio-methanol (engine conversion)
scenarios.note: Engine conversion or newbuild plus bunkering at both terminals.

scenarios.label: Shore power at berth and anchorage
scenarios.note: Cold ironing at both terminals plus a connection for vessels queueing offshore. Displaces only the stationary hotel load, but that is the single largest block of energy on this corridor and it needs no change to the ships' propulsion.

scenarios.label: Battery-electric, PLN grid
scenarios.note: Shore energy at the industrial tariff. Ship-side CO2 follows the grid; all ship-side NOx, SOx, PM and black carbon go to zero at the two terminals.

scenarios.label: Battery-electric, dedicated RE
scenarios.note: Same energy from dedicated renewables plus storage at the terminals.

assumptions.note: [ASSUM] Activity is assumed, not observed. Obtaining AIS for the other ASDP routes is the single highest-value next data step.

activity_week.note: Every crossing this vessel made in one week, drawn to scale on a 168-hour axis. The gaps are time alongside.

sanity_checks.basis: IMO baseline SFC for medium-speed engines is 205-215 g/kWh, rising about 18% at the low loads seen on this crossing.
Marine four-stroke diesels convert 40-45% of fuel energy to shaft work at design load, less at part load.
Ro-pax ferries typically carry 0.4-1.0 kW per GT depending on service speed.
Published Merak-Bakauheni schedules give 15 nm in 90-120 minutes: 7.5-10 knots on the regular berths, up to 15 knots on the executive service.
A 5,000 GT ferry on a 2-3 hour crossing would be expected to burn roughly 0.2-1.0 t, i.e. 0.04-0.20 t per 1,000 GT.
Ro-pax is among the least efficient classes per GT-nm: it carries volume rather than mass on short high-frequency services. A 15 nm crossing sits high in the range ICCT reports for this class.

For ro-pax on very short crossings with long turnarounds, hotel and vehicle-deck ventilation load is a large share of total energy; the Fourth IMO GHG Study finds auxiliary demand comparable to propulsion for some passenger classes.
Black carbon is a meaningful but not dominant share of 100-year warming from residual-fuel four-stroke engines at low load. It is larger on a 20-year horizon.

sanity_checks.check: Share of port-to-port time spent waiting
sanity_checks.basis: The corridor has roughly 28 berth slots against about 70 available ships, and vessels are reported queueing at anchor for hours at peak.

power.note: Displacement from LOA x beam x draft x Cb where reported, else from a log-log fit of displacement on GT. Propulsion power at sea uses the Admiralty relation at the OBSERVED steaming speed with the ICCT correction factors (hull fouling, weather, draught) applied multiplicatively, so the register's unreliable design-speed field does not propagate into the fuel estimate. Installed MCR is estimated at design speed and used only for the load factor, the manoeuvring floor and battery sizing.

prices.domestic_fuel_source: [MKT] Pertamina non-subsidised industrial 'harga keekonomian', 15-31 March 2026 period, as reported by fuel distributors. This was an oil-price spike fortnight (Brent above USD 100) and is NOT a good annual planning number. Verify against ASDP's own bunker invoices before use.
prices.intl_fuel_source: [MKT] Singapore VLSFO ranged roughly USD 780-850/t and MGO USD 1,100-1,220/t through August 2026; VLSFO briefly exceeded USD 1,000/t in March 2026.
prices.biofuel_source: [MKT] Singapore B30-VLSFO premium over conventional VLSFO reported at USD 231/t (late Aug 2026). Rotterdam B100 around USD 1,387/t (late Jul 2026).
prices.pln_source: [GOV] PLN non-subsidised tariff schedule; rates frozen through Q3 2026.
prices.methanol_source: [ASSUM] indicative; bio-methanol is thinly traded and site-specific.

assumptions.fx_source: [MKT] Mid-market USD/IDR 17,900 on 11 September 2026 (50-day average 17,927; 52-week range 16,095 to 18,180).

grid.source: [ASSUM] Indonesian grid emission factors for the JAMALI and Sumatra systems are commonly quoted in the 0.75-0.90 tCO2/MWh range. NOT VERIFIED against a current MEMR/ESDM decree. Must be replaced with the official grid emission factor for the relevant system year before publication.

electric.battery_cost_source: [LIT] Marine battery systems reported at USD 800-1,000/kWh for retrofits and around USD 500/kWh for newbuilds (DNV, via sustainable-ships.org, 2025). Cell prices have fallen further since; treat as an upper bound.

assumptions.pathway_source: [LIT/ASSUM] B40: 40% FAME by volume, biogenic CO2 counted zero tank-to-wake, and the bio fraction assigned a 60% well-to-wake saving, giving about 24% overall. B100/HVO: 80% well-to-wake saving, typical of waste-oil feedstocks under RED II style accounting. Bio-methanol: 85%. Electric-on-grid is computed from the grid emission factor, not assumed. Feedstock availability and certification are NOT modelled and are the binding constraint in practice.
assumptions.terminology: SAF (sustainable aviation fuel) is an aviation product and is not used in shipping. The marine equivalents modelled here are FAME biodiesel (B40, which Indonesia already mandates on land), HVO/B100 renewable diesel, and bio- or e-methanol.

route_distance.name: Merak (Java) - Bakauheni (Sumatra)
route_distance.distance_nm_source: [LIT] Indonesian ferry-operations literature consistently states the Bakauheni-Merak crossing as 15 miles (nautical), with scheduled sailing times of 90-120 minutes depending on berth. Great-circle distance between the two port coordinates is 15.1 nm, which corroborates this.

method_sources.primary: Olmer, N., Comer, B., Roy, B., Mao, X., & Rutherford, D. (2017). Greenhouse gas emissions from global shipping, 2013-2015: Detailed methodology. ICCT. Auxiliary power by class and phase (App. C), boiler power (App. D), main and auxiliary engine emission factors (App. E, G), black carbon factors (App. F), low-load adjustment factors (App. I), draught adjustment factors (Table 13), hull fouling after Townsin (2000, 2003), weather factor.
method_sources.imo: Third IMO GHG Study 2014 (Smith et al.) and Fourth IMO GHG Study 2020 (Faber et al.): activity-based bottom-up structure, SFOC load curve, low-load factors.
method_sources.cf: IMO Resolution MEPC.281(70) Table 1: carbon conversion factors and heating values.
method_sources.gwp: IPCC AR4 for CH4 and N2O; Bond et al. (2013) for black carbon.
method_sources.corbett: Corbett, Wang & Winebrake (2009), Transp. Res. D 14(8): speed reduction abatement costs, USD 30-200 per tonne CO2 for the container fleet, used here as a reference point for judging the abatement costs reported below. Winebrake, Corbett, Wang, Farrell & Woods (2005), JAWMA 55(4): fleetwide emissions reduction optimisation for passenger ferries, the closest published analogue to this task.
method_sources.wb: World Bank Pacific Observatory, Greenhouse Gas Emissions from Maritime Traffic: the Bank's own implementation of the same IMO method on AIS data.
